item.title: Explain a Design Jury's Trade-Off
item.audience: entrants and readers of a civic design competition
item.prompt_text: A jury must explain why it selected a modular shade structure over a sleeker entry for a small public square. The modular entry allows individual panels to be removed for repairs. It uses standard fittings and will look less uniform as panels are replaced. The other proposal offers better initial shade coverage and a continuous silhouette. Write a public statement that makes the winning criterion explicit, acknowledges what the alternative did better, and says what would make the jury reverse its decision.
item.target_grammar: Concession, counterfactuals and calibrated qualification; precise comparative language.
item.target_structure: Outcome and criterion → comparison → accountable implementation condition → genuine reversal condition.

checklist.point: State the decision and the reason it matters over time.
Acknowledge the competing entry's substantive strengths.
Explain the aesthetic downside and a workable way to handle it.
Give a credible fact or circumstance that would reverse the decision.
